How do you reconcile libertarian ideals of property rights with the protection of the environment? I get that property rights incentivize taking care of your own property, but I'm more specifically asking about pollution. If you dump toxins into the air or water supply, would that count as infringement of another's property rights, or exercise of your own? Any links to further reading is appreciated.

I think the easiest thing to consider is that if you dump pollution on your land, it's likely to migrate to your neighbors land and now you've violated his\her property rights. So your rights end when they infringe on someone elses rights. Simple.

If you can demonstrate damage to your property from my dumping to a court that agrees with your assessment, you'll be awarded a favorable judgment against me. My dumping my even result in many such suits being levied. The example would set a precedent that dissuades other dumpers who now realize it's more valuable to not dump shit wherever they want.

That said, if the damage is insignificant, trivial and otherwise unproven, and you still insist on bringing suit, you may not find a court willing to hear the case. If you persist, I might even win a suit against you for harassment when it becomes clear that you don't have a real case but won't relent.

Finally, "protection of the environment" is not a libertarian ideal. It may or may not be an ideal embraced by a community and it's up to an individual and his peers to decide--independently of one another--whether that ideal has value in practice over the other needs and wants they have in life.

You made a mistake, you forgot to multiply the 3600 seconds of an hour by 24 hours of the day.

year = 365 days
day = 24 hours
hour = 60 minutes
minute = 60 seconds

460699 NCIC entries per year / 365 days = 1262 NCIC entries per day
1262 NCIC entries per day / 24 hours = 53 NCIC entries per hour
53 NCIC entries per hour / 60 minutes = 0.88 NCIC entries per minute
0.88 NCIC entries per minute / 60 seconds = 0.0146 NCIC entries per second
